text: Area 77 is Hyderabad's only experiential learning destination of its kind — a 150-acre protected reserve where agriculture, recreation, education, and adventure come together in one immersive environment. The name stands for A-R-E-A: Agriculture, Recreation, Education, Adventure. Set amid rich flora and fauna and a thriving Miyawaki afforestation zone, Area 77 offers curated, ticketed experiences that let visitors learn by doing rather than simply observe. It suits family outings, school field trips, corporate offsites, or a quiet morning walk.
Area 77 quick facts: 150 acres of protected reserve, over 50 bird species visit the property, and farm access is open 365 days a year. It is a strictly plastic-free environmental sanctuary.

Agriculture is the beating heart of Area 77. Using modern farming technology, the reserve cultivates exotic produce — strawberries, avocados, cherries, and more — in open farms in Hyderabad. Activities include: farm-to-hand picking experiences (strawberry picking, sunflower picking, and seasonal fruit/vegetable picking through the year); half-day and full-day corporate and school programs; hands-on "plow, till, sow, and harvest" farming with the team; a working dairy and poultry farm; animal feeding and bird watching (50+ bird species); a working honeybee farm where visitors learn how honey is made; and a walking/running track open every day through the farm and forest.

The recreation zone at Area 77 is built for visitors of every age and includes: a 16-hole mini golf course, an RC car racing track, an RC car crawling track, RC boat racing on the lake, and an outdoor arcade. The entire recreation zone doubles as a venue for birthday parties and corporate retreats.

Area 77 offers structured educational programming for all age groups, blending curriculum-linked learning with hands-on nature immersion: an Advanced Learner's Program for high school students integrated with classroom study; practical lessons on farming and its benefits; introductory botanical studies on flowers, vegetables, and fruits; naturalist-led nature walks explaining the property's flora; themed gardens including the Spice Garden, Herbal Garden, Tulsi Garden, Rose Garden, and Nakshatra Garden; a Buddha Garden dedicated to quiet meditation; and an Open-Air Reading Garden for reading and unwinding.

For visitors seeking a physical challenge, Area 77 offers a 7-obstacle rope course (about 60 minutes to complete), cycling trails, hiking routes, trail exploring, and guided exploration of the on-site Miyawaki forest — a dense, fast-grown microforest planted using the Miyawaki method, with a noticeably different microclimate from the rest of the reserve.

Area 77 is also a premier event space with three settings across three scales: the Lakeside Lawn & Cabana Venue, an intimate waterfront setting suited to dinners and small weddings for 150–200 guests; the Bamboo Shelter & Central Lawn, the largest venue, an open central lawn beneath a bamboo shelter for big-scale celebrations of 300–500 guests; and the Recreational Zone (RC cars, mini golf, RC boats, adventure course, cycling, animal feeding), bookable for kids' birthday parties and corporate retreats.
## Berry & Bean — the café at Area 77

Berry & Bean is Area 77's in-house specialty coffee house — a lakeside café serving its own tea and coffee blends. It has lakeside seating right along the water, and every other Area 77 activity (mini golf, RC cars and boats, cycling) is within walking distance of the table, making it a place to work, relax, or socialise between activities.

# Area 77 school & outdoor experiential learning programs

Area 77 runs an Outdoor Experiential Learning Program for schools, eco-clubs, and summer camps, redefining education through experiential learning, physical challenges, agricultural science, and artistic expression.
## Key guidelines for school management

Area 77 is a strictly plastic-free sanctuary. The recommended/required teacher-to-student supervision ratio is 1:25. Any child allergies or medical conditions must be emailed to Area 77 prior to arrival so support arrangements can be made. Catering is optional — programs can be booked with or without a meal plan. Cycling and mini-golf are add-on activities and must be specified at the time of booking.
## Grade-level structure
Primary School (Ages 4–10, focus: Sensory & Motor Skills): tactile farming, animal feeding empathy, entry-level obstacle courses, guided plant discovery, mini-golf play, and lakeside nature art.
Middle School (Ages 11–13, focus: Dynamics & Ecology): farm-to-table experience, elevated ropes obstacles, soil science, botanical cycles, cycling paths, and lakeside nature painting.

High School (Ages 14+, focus: Leadership & Resilience): advanced high-ropes navigation, strategic leadership challenges, in-depth agricultural concepts, environmental mindfulness, animal care, and creative reset sessions.
## Program core pillars
1. STEM & Ecology: farm-to-table concepts, strawberry harvests, soil health, botanical walks, ecological exploration, and ethical animal care.
2. Action & Leadership: high-energy rope courses, collaborative group problem solving, mini-golf geometry and sportsmanship, and cycling on open-air tracks.
3. Arts & Well-Being: lakeside nature canvas painting, open-air art workshops, and environmental mindfulness walks that help alleviate academic stress and reduce anxiety.

9:00–9:30 AM Arrival & Welcome Orientation (safety briefing, team grouping, hydration check); 9:30–11:30 AM Rotation A — Adventure & Agriculture (high-rope obstacle course & team building, or farm cultivation & animal care); 11:30 AM–12:00 PM hydration/snack pause; 12:00–1:30 PM Rotation B — Botanical & Strategy (botanical walk & crop picking, or mini-golf tournament & cycling); 1:30–2:30 PM in-house chef buffet lunch; 2:30–3:40 PM Sensory & Creative Expression (lakeside canvas painting, mindfulness walk); 3:40–4:15 PM Reflection & Departure Wrap-Up.
## Curriculum alignment

The program bridges textbook theory and real-world application. For IGCSE students, the Miyawaki Forest is a case study for Environmental Management and Biology (urban afforestation, carbon sinks, indigenous biodiversity). For IB students, it aligns with Environmental Systems and Societies (ESS) — analyzing the multi-layered Miyawaki forest structure for Succession and Intraspecific Competition, useful as primary data for Internal Assessments. It also supports IB CAS (Creativity, Activity, Service): Creativity via documenting forest growth or designing an "Eco-Trail" guide; Activity via rope courses and physical farming tasks; Service via participation in sustainable organic agriculture and biodiversity maintenance.
## Food & catering for school groups

Area 77 offers end-to-end dining/catering: in-house buffet services with fresh, hygienic, student-friendly menus prepared on site; customizable menu styles (high-nutrition continental spreads or traditional regional formats) to suit dietary needs; hydration hubs with continuous water/refreshment stations along activity tracks; and full staff support (dedicated setup, serving, and cleanup crews) so teachers can focus on supervision rather than logistics.
## Laid-Back Experience Package / Advanced Explorer's Program

Price: ₹2,499. Designed as a serene, relaxed alternative blending nature, relaxation, and gentle activities. Inclusions: a guided walking tour through the property's trails; breakfast by the lake; bicycle rental & cycling; water stream exploration with quiet reflection time; and an animal feeding session.

Area77 Club is described as an exclusive escape into nature's luxury — a retreat blending wellness with world-class refinement, featuring ethically sourced dining, a specialty coffee house, and spa-grade shower facilities.
## School registration form — information needed to book

To book a school visit, Area 77's Education Program Coordinators need: school name and date of proposed visit; contact person/coordinator name, phone number and email; estimated student count and accompanying teacher count by grade level (Primary Ages 4–10, Middle Ages 11–13, High School Ages 14+); which program/package is wanted (Sample Day Excursion Schedule, Advanced Young Explorer's Program at ₹2,499, Laid-Back Experience Package, or a Custom Multi-Pillar Program); any optional add-ons (Mini-Golf Greens Tournament, Cycling & Open-Air Tracks, Pottery Wheel Workshop); catering/meal preference (full in-house buffet lunch, continental menu style, traditional regional format, no catering/program only, or special dietary/medical requirements detailed by email); and a signed declaration acknowledging the plastic-free policy and the 1:25 teacher-to-student supervision ratio. Schools should contact Area 77's Education Program Coordinators to schedule a site walkthrough, review custom menu packages, or tailor a day-out itinerary to their curriculum objectives.
